meta.description: Runs the MS-DIAL preprocessing workflow (peak picking, MS2Dec spectral deconvolution, alignment, gap-filling) and imports the alignment-result table into R or Python with honest filtering. Use when preprocessing LC-MS DDA/DIA (SWATH) or GC-MS raw data with MS-DIAL, deciding MS-DIAL vs XCMS, configuring the MSDIALCUI console run, or parsing an MS-DIAL export into a clean feature matrix.
meta.n_inputs_note: 5 inputs (1-5) are the pre-fix report's own inputs, re-run here as regression tests; inputs 6-7 are new, added per the re-audit brief so the score is not measured only against defects the fixer already knew about. Complexity is unchanged (Moderate scope) but N=7 to satisfy the regression+new-input requirement.

practice_boundaries.detail: Preprocessing pipeline for aggregate metabolomics data; no individual-subject diagnostic or prescriptive content in any output.

recommendations.title: Malformed param-file syntax (Key=Value) fails silently, not loudly
recommendations.problem: A param-file line using the old MS-DIAL 4 style 'Key=Value' instead of the documented 'Key: Value' is not rejected by the real console -- it is silently dropped and the console falls back to its built-in default for that key, exits 0, and prints no warning. Verified with a controlled comparison: an extreme 'Minimum peak height: 500000' correctly cut 11605 features down to 13, but the identical value written as 'Minimum peak height=500000' produced 11605 features -- byte-identical to not setting it at all.
recommendations.root_cause: SKILL.md's Common Errors table documents the Key=Value mistake as a generic symptom ('filter keeps 0/all features') rather than warning that the console gives zero error signal when it happens, so a researcher has no way to know their run silently used defaults instead of their intended parameters.
recommendations.fix: Add an explicit Common Errors / Reliability row: 'A malformed or misspelled param-file key (e.g. Key=Value instead of Key: Value, or a typo'd key name) is silently ignored by the console -- exit code 0, no warning, defaults used instead. Always spot-check a run by deliberately varying one known parameter (e.g. Minimum peak height) and confirming the feature count actually changes, rather than trusting a clean exit code alone.'

recommendations.title: Targeted MRM/PRM/SRM quantification is never routed to metabolomics/targeted-analysis
recommendations.problem: The repository has a sibling metabolomics/targeted-analysis Skill, and the real installed console exposes its own -t/--target flag for single-compound target-mode processing, but neither is mentioned anywhere in msdial-preprocessing's SKILL.md or usage-guide.md, including the otherwise-thorough 'When NOT to Use This Skill' section.
recommendations.root_cause: The 'When NOT to Use' section was written to cover the 4 sibling Skills known at the time; it was not revisited when -t/target-mode support or the targeted-analysis Skill entered scope.
recommendations.fix: Add one line to 'When NOT to Use This Skill' and 'Related Skills': 'Fixed panel of known targets / MRM-PRM-SRM quantification -> metabolomics/targeted-analysis (MSDIALCUI.exe also exposes a -t/--target flag for single-compound target mode; this Skill's untargeted alignment is for discovery, not a predefined target list).'

recommendations.title: The per-file acquisition_type CSV mechanism is documented but never empirically confirmed against real DIA data

recommendations.root_cause: No real DIA/ABF test data exists in this candidate's audit environment (per TOOLS.md), so neither the fixer nor this audit could close the loop on this specific claim.
recommendations.fix: Add a one-sentence caveat next to the CSV acquisition_type instructions noting it is sourced from the official tutorial and CLI-mechanism-verified, but not yet confirmed against a real DIA/SWATH run's MS2Dec output; revisit once ABF/DIA test data is available.
